title: USPS Carries Nearly Half Its Peak Mail, Yet Stamps Cost More
hook: Fewer letters made mailing one more expensive, not cheaper.
closing: Every mailbox costs money to reach, even when fewer letters help fund the trip.
question: What do you still mail?

segments.say: USPS mail fell to 109 billion pieces, leaving the network with nearly half its former traffic.
First-Class Mail fell to 46 billion pieces, showing letters disappeared fastest.
A stamp reached 68 cents, because shrinking volume did not shrink the nationwide delivery network.
